display.title: Episode 139: The Sound of the Shofar (Rosh Chodesh Elul)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Elul, Uncle Yossi explains the wake-up call of the shofar and tells the parable of a village boy who thought a bugle could put out a fire.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Elul. Uncle Yossi welcomes listeners back from summer camp and asks them to tell their classes about the program. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, he plays the sound of the shofar heard every morning in Elul and explains that it is an alarm: a month to prepare for the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah by improving our thoughts, our speech (no lashon hara, careful davening, three chapters of Tehillim a day) and our actions, especially daily tzedakah. An eight-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema. Story time explains, in the words of the Rambam, that the shofar of Rosh Hashanah wakes us from sleep, then tells a parable: a village plagued by fires sends a farm boy to the big city, where he sees the fire chief blow a bugle from a tower. Back home he blows a bugle while the houses burn, until the fire chief explains that the bugle is only a signal to run for water. So too the shofar calls us to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. The show ends with wishes for a good and sweet year.
display.lesson: The shofar is an alarm, not the cure: it wakes us up to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

date.note: On air: 'today is Rosh Chodesh Elul' and the shofar will be blown 'tomorrow morning'. Tuesday 30 Av 5744 = 28 Aug 1984; consistent with episode 138 (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul).

sources_cited.note: Quoted as the Torah's command to sound the shofar.
The shofar is a heavenly decree, yet hints at an alarm waking the sleepers.
